question: Should Gateway browser-origin authorization accept scheme-level wildcard entries such as `chrome-extension://*`, and if so what exact pattern grammar and limits should be supported?
rationale: This changes which browser origins may reach Gateway HTTP/WebSocket handling, and the current documented contract intentionally allows only full origins plus the global `*` escape hatch.

options.title: Approve a constrained grammar
options.body: Define a small documented pattern contract, implement it in the shared origin helper, and cover allowed, rejected, exact, global wildcard, WebSocket, and trusted-proxy HTTP cases.

options.title: Keep exact origins only
options.body: Reject scheme wildcards for this boundary and rely on exact opaque-origin fixes plus the built-in Chrome extension relay for supported extension workflows.

options.title: Defer to pattern-design work
options.body: Wait for the constrained loopback-pattern contract to settle, then decide whether Chrome extension scheme wildcards belong in that same surface or a separate one.

recommendation.title: Approve a constrained grammar
recommendation.body: Define a small documented pattern contract, implement it in the shared origin helper, and cover allowed, rejected, exact, global wildcard, WebSocket, and trusted-proxy HTTP cases.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the origin-check boundary and owns the nearest current Chrome extension relay direction, making him the strongest routing candidate for the security decision.
